situation_en: You walk into a café near campus. Order an iced americano to go, decline the loyalty points, and pay by card.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Welcome. Are you ready to order?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: One iced americano, please.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: What size would you like?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 큰 사이즈로 주세요. 얼음 조금만 넣어 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: Keun saijeuro juseyo. Eoreum jogeumman neoeo juseyo.
dialogue.en: A large, please. Just a little ice, please.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: For here?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: No, I'll take it to go.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Would you like to collect points?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: No points, thanks. Can I pay by card?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.ko: 네, 카드 꽂아 주세요. 영수증 드릴까요?
dialogue.romanization: Ne, kadeu kkoja juseyo. Yeongsujeung deurilkkayo?
dialogue.en: Yes, please insert your card. Would you like the receipt?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: You can throw the receipt away.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Come and pick it up when the buzzer rings.

chunks.note: Pattern: [item] + [number] + [counter] + 주세요. 잔 is the counter for cups and glasses.
chunks.common_mistake: 하나 잔 ✗ → 한 잔 ✓. 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷 shorten to 한, 두, 세, 네 before a counter.

chunks.note: (으)로 주세요 = 'I'll have it as …'. Use it to choose an option: size, hot or iced, card or cash.
chunks.common_mistake: Use 로 after a vowel (사이즈로) and 으로 after a consonant (현금으로).

chunks.note: -만 = 'only/just'. 얼음 빼 주세요 = no ice, 샷 추가해 주세요 = add a shot.
chunks.common_mistake: 넣어 주세요 means 'put in'. Without 조금만 you are asking for ice, not less ice.

chunks.note: Staff usually ask 드시고 가세요? (eating here?). 테이크아웃이요 is also very common in cafés.
chunks.common_mistake: Answering 네 to 드시고 가세요? means you are staying. Say 아니요, 가져갈게요.

chunks.note: Literally 'I'll eat and then go'. Koreans say 먹고 갈게요 even for drinks.
chunks.common_mistake: 여기 있어요 means 'here you are' (handing something over), not 'for here'.

chunks.note: 괜찮아요 is the polite way to say 'no thank you' to any offer: bag, receipt, points.
chunks.common_mistake: Saying 아니요 alone sounds abrupt. 괜찮아요 is softer.

chunks.note: [noun] 돼요? = 'Is … possible?' Works for 와이파이 돼요?, 포장 돼요?, 할인 돼요?
chunks.common_mistake: 되요 ✗ → 돼요 ✓. 돼 is short for 되어. Even many Koreans make this spelling mistake.

chunks.en: You can throw the receipt away.
chunks.note: Very common in Korea. Staff will ask 영수증 드릴까요? after you pay.
chunks.common_mistake: 버리세요 sounds like an order. -아/어 주세요 is a polite request.

chunks.note: Same pattern for the restroom code: 화장실 비밀번호가 뭐예요? Many cafés lock their restrooms.
chunks.common_mistake: 뭐에요 ✗ → 뭐예요 ✓. After a vowel, use 예요.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Welcome. Are you ready to order?
roleplay.task_en: Order one hot latte.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Ask for the small size.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Say yes, you'll have it here.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Would you like to collect points?
roleplay.task_en: Politely decline.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: How would you like to pay?
roleplay.task_en: Ask if you can pay by card.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Ask them to throw it away.

situation_en: You just arrived at Busan Station and want to go to Haeundae Beach. Ask for directions, top up your transit card, and find the right exit.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Excuse me, how do I get to Haeundae?

dialogue.speaker: 행인
dialogue.ko: 지하철 타면 돼요. 1호선 타고 서면역에서 2호선으로 갈아타세요.
dialogue.romanization: Jihacheol tamyeon dwaeyo. Ilhoseon tago seomyeonyeogeseo ihoseoneuro garataseyo.
dialogue.en: Take the subway. Take Line 1 and transfer to Line 2 at Seomyeon Station.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Is it far from here?

dialogue.speaker: 행인
dialogue.ko: 좀 멀어요. 한 시간 정도 걸려요.
dialogue.romanization: Jom meoreoyo. Han sigan jeongdo geollyeoyo.
dialogue.en: It's a bit far. It takes about an hour.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Thank you!

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: (At a convenience store) Please top up my transit card.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: How much?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: 10,000 won, please.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: (해운대역에서) 해수욕장에 가려면 몇 번 출구로 나가야 돼요?
dialogue.romanization: (Haeundaeyeogeseo) Haesuyokjange garyeomyeon myeot beon chulguro nagaya dwaeyo?
dialogue.en: (At Haeundae Station) Which exit should I take to get to the beach?

dialogue.speaker: 역무원
dialogue.en: Go out Exit 5 and go straight.

chunks.en: How do I get to Haeundae?
chunks.note: Pattern: [place]에 어떻게 가요? Start with 저기요 (excuse me) to get a stranger's attention.
chunks.common_mistake: 해운대에서 ✗ → 해운대에 ✓. 에서 means 'from/at', 에 means 'to'.

chunks.note: Answer you may hear: 가까워요 (it's close), 걸어서 10분 걸려요 (10 minutes on foot).
chunks.common_mistake: 멀어요 comes from 멀다. Don't confuse it with 많아요 (there are a lot).

chunks.note: Busan has subway lines 1–4. 호선 = line number. -아야/어야 돼요 = 'have to'.
chunks.common_mistake: Use 타다 (to ride) for subways, buses and taxis, not 가다.

chunks.note: Signs and announcements use 환승 (transfer). 갈아타다 is the everyday verb.
chunks.common_mistake: Transferring between bus and subway within 30 minutes is free with a transit card. Always tap out (하차 태그).

chunks.en: Please top up my transit card.
chunks.note: Convenience stores (편의점) and subway machines top up cards. Most stores take cash only for top-ups.
chunks.common_mistake: 충전 also means charging a phone: 휴대폰 충전할 수 있어요? = Can I charge my phone?

chunks.note: Money uses Sino-Korean numbers: 오천 원, 만 원, 이만 원.
chunks.common_mistake: 일만 원 ✗ → 만 원 ✓. Koreans drop 일 before 만, 천 and 백.

chunks.note: Station exits are numbered, and maps and friends will say '○번 출구 앞에서 만나요'.
chunks.common_mistake: 출구 = exit, 입구 = entrance. Exit numbers are read with Sino-Korean numbers: 오 번 출구.

chunks.note: Use this on a crowded bus or subway. On buses, press the 하차 (stop) bell before your stop.
chunks.common_mistake: 내려요 states a fact. 내릴게요 tells people around you what you are about to do.

chunks.note: Pattern: [place](으)로 가 주세요. Showing the address on Kakao Map also works.
chunks.common_mistake: Use 으로 after a consonant: 해운대역으로, but 서면으로 / 광안리로.

roleplay.speaker: 행인
roleplay.task_en: Ask how to get to Gwangalli (광안리).

roleplay.speaker: 행인
roleplay.prompt_ko: 지하철 타면 돼요. 한 번 갈아타야 돼요.
roleplay.prompt_en: Take the subway. You need to transfer once.
roleplay.task_en: Ask where you transfer.

roleplay.speaker: 행인
roleplay.prompt_en: Transfer to Line 2 at Seomyeon Station.
roleplay.task_en: Ask if it's far from here.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: (Convenience store) How can I help you?
roleplay.task_en: Ask them to top up your transit card.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Say 20,000 won.

roleplay.speaker: 버스
roleplay.prompt_ko: (버스 안. 사람이 많아요. 다음 정류장에서 내려야 돼요.)
roleplay.prompt_en: (On a crowded bus. You need to get off at the next stop.)
roleplay.task_en: Politely say you're getting off.

roleplay.speaker: 기사님
roleplay.task_en: Ask to go to Gwangalli Beach (광안리 해수욕장).

situation_en: Lunch with a friend at a 돼지국밥 (pork soup) restaurant near campus. Get a table for two, order it not spicy, ask for more kimchi, and pay separately.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Welcome. How many of you?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Two.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Have a seat here. What can I get you?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Two pork soups, please.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Would you like it spicy?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: No, not spicy, please.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: OK, it'll be right out.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Excuse me, a bit more kimchi, please.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.ko: 반찬은 저기서 셀프로 가져가시면 돼요. 맛있게 드세요.
dialogue.romanization: Banchaneun jeogiseo selpeuro gajyeogasimyeon dwaeyo. Masitge deuseyo.
dialogue.en: Side dishes are self-service over there. Enjoy your meal.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Thank you. (Let's eat!)

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Shall I put it on one bill?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: No, can we pay separately?

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Sure, one card at a time.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Thank you for the meal!

chunks.note: 명 counts people. Staff ask politely with 분: 몇 분이세요? You answer with 명 for yourselves.
chunks.common_mistake: 둘 명 ✗ → 두 명 ✓ (하나, 둘, 셋 become 한, 두, 세 before a counter).

chunks.note: 돼지국밥 is Busan's signature dish. 개 is the all-purpose counter; 그릇 counts bowls.
chunks.common_mistake: 두 돼지국밥 ✗ → 돼지국밥 두 개 ✓: the number comes after the noun.

chunks.note: -게 해 주세요 = make it …: 안 맵게 (not spicy), 덜 맵게 (less spicy), 맵게 (spicy).
chunks.common_mistake: 맵지 않아 주세요 ✗ → 안 맵게 해 주세요 ✓

chunks.note: How you call staff in a Korean restaurant. Many tables also have a call bell.
chunks.common_mistake: 아줌마! can sound rude. 저기요 or 사장님 is safer.

alternatives: 김치 좀 더 주실 수 있어요?
chunks.note: Side dishes (반찬) are free and refillable. 좀 더 = a bit more.
chunks.common_mistake: 김치 하나 더 ✗ for a refill → 김치 좀 더 주세요 ✓

chunks.en: (before eating) Thank you for the food.
chunks.note: Said before you start eating, especially when someone treats you.
chunks.common_mistake: Don't mix it up with 잘 먹었습니다, which is said after the meal.

chunks.note: In most Korean restaurants you pay at the counter (카운터) on the way out.
chunks.common_mistake: 빌 주세요 ✗: Koreans don't use 'bill'. Say 계산해 주세요.

chunks.note: 따로 = separately; 같이 = together. Splitting the bill is common among students.
chunks.common_mistake: 다르게 계산 ✗ → 따로 계산 ✓

chunks.en: Thank you for the meal. (after eating)
chunks.note: Said to the staff or owner when you leave. They love hearing it.
chunks.common_mistake: 잘 먹겠습니다 (future) is for before the meal.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Say three people.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Order two 밀면 (Busan's cold wheat noodles).

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Ask for it less spicy.

roleplay.speaker: 식당
roleplay.prompt_en: (You finished the side dishes. Call the staff.)
roleplay.task_en: Call the staff and ask for more 깍두기 (radish kimchi).

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Say what Koreans say before eating.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Ask to pay separately.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Thank them for the meal as you leave.

situation_en: At the convenience store under your dorm: get your lunchbox heated, grab a 1+1 deal, say you don't need a bag, pay with your transit card, and pick up a parcel.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Welcome.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 이 도시락 데워 주실 수 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: I dosirak dewo jusil su isseoyo?
dialogue.en: Could you heat up this lunchbox?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.ko: 전자레인지는 저쪽에 있어요. 직접 데우시면 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: Jeonjareinjineun jeojjoge isseoyo. Jikjeop deusimyeon dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: The microwave is over there. You can heat it yourself.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Oh, OK. And this too, please.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.ko: 이 음료수는 원 플러스 원이에요. 하나 더 가져오세요.
dialogue.romanization: I eumnyosuneun won peulleoseu wonieyo. Hana deo gajyeooseyo.
dialogue.en: This drink is buy one get one free. Grab another one.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Really? Thank you!

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Do you need a bag?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: No, I don't need a bag.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: That's 4,200 won.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Can I pay with a transit card?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Yes, tap it here.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Also, I came to pick up a parcel.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: May I have your name?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: It's Alex.

chunks.note: 데우다 = to warm up. -아/어 주실 수 있어요? is a polite request. In many stores you use the microwave yourself.
chunks.common_mistake: 데워요 주세요 ✗ → 데워 주세요 ✓

chunks.note: 전자레인지 = microwave. Short questions like this drop 는 and 에 in speech.
chunks.common_mistake: 마이크로웨이브 isn't used in Korean.

chunks.note: 도 = also. Put an item on the counter and say this.
chunks.common_mistake: 이것 또 ✗ → 이것도 ✓ (도 attaches to the word).

chunks.note: Korean stores love 1+1 and 2+1 deals. Read them in English: 원 플러스 원, 투 플러스 원.
chunks.common_mistake: 일 더하기 일 ✗: that's maths, not a store deal.

chunks.note: 괜찮아요 = 'no thanks'. Bags cost extra (봉투값), so many people bring their own.
chunks.common_mistake: A plain 아니요 can sound curt. Add 괜찮아요.

chunks.en: Can I pay with a transit card?
chunks.note: Most convenience stores take T-money and Cashbee. (으)로 = by means of: 카드로, 현금으로.
chunks.common_mistake: 교통카드에 돼요? ✗ → 교통카드로 돼요? ✓

chunks.en: I came to pick up a parcel.
chunks.note: V-(으)러 왔어요 = I came to V. Many students have parcels delivered to a convenience store.
chunks.common_mistake: 택배를 사러 왔어요 ✗ (to buy a parcel) → 찾으러 ✓

chunks.note: [Item] 있어요? = 'Do you have/sell …?' in any shop.
chunks.common_mistake: 충전기 가지고 있어요? ✗: that asks whether the clerk personally owns one.

chunks.note: Ask for 젓가락 (chopsticks) or 숟가락 (spoon) with a lunchbox or cup noodles.
chunks.common_mistake: 젓가락 두 개 for one pair ✗: a pair is just 젓가락 (하나).

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Ask where the microwave is.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_ko: 저쪽에 있어요. 다른 건 필요 없으세요?
roleplay.task_en: Ask if they have phone chargers.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Yes, over there. Do you need a bag?
roleplay.task_en: Say yes, one bag please.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Ask if you can pay with a transit card.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_ko: 네, 여기 대 주세요. 더 필요한 거 있으세요?
roleplay.prompt_en: Yes, tap it here. Anything else?
roleplay.task_en: Say you came to pick up a parcel.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Shall I heat this lunchbox too?
roleplay.task_en: Say yes, please heat it up.

situation_en: At Jagalchi, Busan's famous fish market: ask the price, get a small discount, buy just half a kilo, and have it sliced to eat upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: 상인
dialogue.ko: 학생, 뭐 찾아요? 오늘 광어 싱싱해요!
dialogue.romanization: Haksaeng, mwo chajayo? Oneul gwangeo singsinghaeyo!
dialogue.en: Student, what are you looking for? The flatfish is fresh today!

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: How much is this?

dialogue.speaker: 상인
dialogue.en: Flatfish is 30,000 won per kilo.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: That's a bit expensive. Could you give me a small discount?

dialogue.speaker: 상인
dialogue.en: Since you're a student, I'll do 28,000 won.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 감사합니다! 반 킬로만 살 수 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: Gamsahamnida! Ban killoman sal su isseoyo?
dialogue.en: Thanks! Can I buy just half a kilo?

dialogue.speaker: 상인
dialogue.en: Then it's 14,000 won.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 회로 먹고 싶어요. 여기서 먹을 수 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: Hoero meokgo sipeoyo. Yeogiseo meogeul su isseoyo?
dialogue.en: I'd like it as sashimi. Can I eat it here?

dialogue.speaker: 상인
dialogue.ko: 회 떠 줄게요. 2층 식당에 가져가면 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: Hoe tteo julgeyo. I cheung sikdange gajyeogamyeon dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: I'll slice it for you. Take it to a restaurant on the second floor.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Do you take cards?

dialogue.speaker: 상인
dialogue.en: Yes. But cash is better.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Then I'll pay in cash.

chunks.note: 싱싱하다 = fresh (fish, vegetables). Vendors love this question.
chunks.common_mistake: 신선해요 is also correct but sounds more formal; 싱싱해요 is the market word.

chunks.note: Point and ask. 이거 = this (near you), 저거 = that (over there).
chunks.common_mistake: 이거 얼마이에요 ✗ → 얼마예요 ✓

chunks.note: N에 = per N: 1킬로에 삼만 원 (30,000 won a kilo). Fish is usually priced by the kilo.
chunks.common_mistake: 1킬로마다 얼마 ✗ (unnatural) → 1킬로에 얼마 ✓

chunks.note: 좀 softens it, a polite way to start bargaining.
chunks.common_mistake: 비싼 이에요 ✗ → 비싸요 ✓ (adjectives conjugate like verbs).

chunks.en: Could you give me a small discount?
chunks.note: Friendly bargaining is normal at traditional markets, but not in shops or chain stores.
chunks.common_mistake: 할인해 주세요 sounds like asking for an official sale. At the market say 깎아 주세요.

chunks.en: Can I buy just half a kilo?
chunks.note: 만 = only. -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요? = is it possible to …?
chunks.common_mistake: 반 킬로 만 ✗: 만 (only) attaches to the word: 반 킬로만.

chunks.note: (으)로 again: 회로 (as sashimi), 구이로 (grilled). 회를 뜨다 = to slice raw fish.
chunks.common_mistake: 회를 먹고 싶어요 is fine too, but 회로 tells the vendor how to prepare it.

chunks.note: At Jagalchi, vendors slice the fish and restaurants upstairs serve it for a small table charge.
chunks.common_mistake: 여기에서 먹을 수 있어요 is also correct; 여기에 먹을 ✗ (actions take 에서).

chunks.note: Small market stalls often prefer cash. 현금 = cash.
chunks.common_mistake: 현금에 할게요 ✗ → 현금으로 ✓

roleplay.speaker: 상인
roleplay.prompt_en: Student, what are you looking for?
roleplay.task_en: Ask what's fresh today.

roleplay.speaker: 상인
roleplay.task_en: Ask how much the squid is per kilo.

roleplay.speaker: 상인
roleplay.task_en: Say it's a bit expensive and ask for a small discount.

roleplay.speaker: 상인
roleplay.task_en: Ask to buy only half a kilo.

roleplay.speaker: 상인
roleplay.prompt_en: OK. Shall I make it sashimi?
roleplay.task_en: Say yes, you'd like it as sashimi.

roleplay.speaker: 상인
roleplay.task_en: Say you'll pay in cash anyway.

situation_en: You have a sore throat and a fever. At a pharmacy near campus, explain your symptoms, say you have no allergies, ask how to take the medicine, and pay.

dialogue.speaker: 약사
dialogue.en: Welcome. What's wrong?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 감기에 걸린 것 같아요. 목이 아프고 기침이 나요.
dialogue.romanization: Gamgie geollin geot gatayo. Mogi apeugo gichimi nayo.
dialogue.en: I think I caught a cold. My throat hurts and I'm coughing.

dialogue.speaker: 약사
dialogue.en: Do you have a fever too?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Yes, I've had a slight fever since last night.

dialogue.speaker: 약사
dialogue.en: Are you allergic to any medicine?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: No, I don't have any allergies.

dialogue.speaker: 약사
dialogue.en: Then take this cold medicine.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: How many times a day do I take it?

dialogue.speaker: 약사
dialogue.ko: 하루 세 번, 식사 후 30분에 드세요.
dialogue.romanization: Haru se beon, siksa hu samsip bune deuseyo.
dialogue.en: Three times a day, 30 minutes after a meal.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Will this medicine make me sleepy?

dialogue.speaker: 약사
dialogue.ko: 조금 졸릴 수 있어요. 운전은 하지 마세요.
dialogue.romanization: Jogeum jollil su isseoyo. Unjeoneun haji maseyo.
dialogue.en: It may make you a little sleepy. Don't drive.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: OK, I understand. How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: I'll pay by card.

chunks.en: I think I caught a cold.
chunks.note: -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 = 'I think…', softer than a flat statement. 감기에 걸리다 = to catch a cold.
chunks.common_mistake: 감기를 잡았어요 ✗ (translated from English) → 감기에 걸렸어요 ✓

chunks.note: [Body part]이/가 아파요: 머리가 아파요 (head), 배가 아파요 (stomach), 이가 아파요 (tooth).
chunks.common_mistake: 제 목이 아파요 isn't wrong, but Korean usually leaves out 'my': 목이 아파요.

chunks.note: 나다 is used for symptoms that 'come out': 기침이 나요, 콧물이 나요 (runny nose), 열이 나요 (fever).
chunks.common_mistake: 기침이 있어요 sounds unnatural → 기침이 나요 or 기침을 해요.

chunks.note: 좀 (a little) softens it. 어젯밤부터 = since last night.
chunks.common_mistake: 몸이 뜨거워요 ✗ for a fever → 열이 나요 ✓

chunks.note: 은/는 here means 'as for allergies': no. To name one: 아스피린 알레르기가 있어요.
chunks.common_mistake: People often say 알러지, but the standard spelling is 알레르기.

chunks.en: How many times a day do I take it?
chunks.note: Medicine is 'eaten' (먹다) in Korean. The pharmacist says the honorific 드세요 to you. On the label you'll see 식후 30분 (30 minutes after meals), short for 식사 후.
chunks.common_mistake: 약을 마셔요 ✗ for pills → 약을 먹어요 ✓

chunks.en: Will this medicine make me sleepy?
chunks.note: -(으)면 = if/when. 졸리다 = to feel sleepy.
chunks.common_mistake: 졸려요 (sleepy) vs 자요 (sleeping): 이 약 먹으면 자요? means 'will I fall asleep?'

chunks.note: Works in every shop. 전부 or 다 해서 = in total.
chunks.common_mistake: 얼마이에요 ✗ → 얼마예요 ✓: after a vowel it's 예요, after a consonant 이에요.

chunks.note: (으)로 할게요 = 'I'll go with…', the same 로/으로 as 큰 사이즈로 주세요. Cash: 현금으로 할게요.
chunks.common_mistake: 카드에 할게요 ✗ → 카드로 할게요 ✓

roleplay.speaker: 약사
roleplay.task_en: Say your stomach hurts.

roleplay.speaker: 약사
roleplay.task_en: Say since this morning.

roleplay.speaker: 약사
roleplay.prompt_en: Do you have a fever too?
roleplay.task_en: Say no, you don't have a fever.

roleplay.speaker: 약사
roleplay.prompt_en: Are you allergic to any medicine?
roleplay.task_en: Say you're allergic to aspirin.

roleplay.speaker: 약사
roleplay.task_en: Ask how many times a day to take it.

roleplay.speaker: 약사
roleplay.prompt_ko: 하루 세 번 드세요. 육천 원입니다.
roleplay.prompt_en: Three times a day. That's 6,000 won.
roleplay.task_en: Say you'll pay in cash.

situation_en: At a language-exchange meetup on campus, a Korean student, Minji, starts talking to you. Introduce yourself, talk about hobbies, suggest going to Gwangalli together, and swap KakaoTalk.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.en: Hi! I'm Minji.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Hi, I'm Alex. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.en: Which country are you from?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 미국에서 왔어요. 부산외대에서 한국어를 공부하고 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: Migugeseo wasseoyo. Busanoedaeeseo hangugeoreul gongbuhago isseoyo.
dialogue.en: I'm from the US. I'm studying Korean at BUFS.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.en: Wow, your Korean is really good!

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Not at all, I still have a lot to learn.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.en: What are your hobbies?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 저는 운동하는 걸 좋아해요. 민지 씨는요?
dialogue.romanization: Jeoneun undonghaneun geol joahaeyo. Minji ssineunyo?
dialogue.en: I like working out. How about you, Minji?

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.ko: 저는 바다 보면서 산책하는 걸 좋아해요.
dialogue.romanization: Jeoneun bada bomyeonseo sanchaekaneun geol joahaeyo.
dialogue.en: I like taking walks by the sea.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 저도 바다 좋아해요! 우리 같이 광안리에 갈래요?
dialogue.romanization: Jeodo bada joahaeyo! Uri gachi Gwanganrie gallaeyo?
dialogue.en: I like the sea too! Shall we go to Gwangalli together?

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.en: Sounds good! Can you give me your KakaoTalk ID?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 네, 제 QR 코드 보여 줄게요.
dialogue.romanization: Ne, je kyuareu kodeu boyeo julgeyo.
dialogue.en: Sure, I'll show you my QR code.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.en: Then I'll message you this weekend!

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 네, 연락 기다릴게요. 오늘 정말 즐거웠어요.
dialogue.romanization: Ne, yeollak gidarilgeyo. Oneul jeongmal jeulgeowosseoyo.
dialogue.en: OK, I'll wait for your message. I really enjoyed today.

chunks.note: The friendly way to say it. 처음 뵙겠습니다 is more formal, for older people or business.
chunks.common_mistake: 반가워요 is only for people you meet, not for things you like.

chunks.note: Answer with [country]에서 왔어요: 베트남에서 왔어요, 미국에서 왔어요.
chunks.common_mistake: 어디 나라 ✗ → 어느 나라 ✓: 어느 = which (one of several).

chunks.note: -고 있어요 = something going on now or these days. Add where: 부산외대에서 한국어를 공부하고 있어요.
chunks.common_mistake: 한국어를 공부해요 is also fine; 한국어를 공부 있어요 ✗ (missing -하고).

chunks.en: Not at all, I still have a lot to learn.
chunks.note: Koreans often brush off a compliment like this. A simple 감사합니다 is fine too.
chunks.common_mistake: 네, 잘해요 sounds like bragging in Korean, even if you mean 'thanks'.

chunks.note: A classic first-meeting question. 취미가 어떻게 되세요? is the politer version.
chunks.common_mistake: 뭐예요 (what is it) vs 뭐해요 (what are you doing): 취미가 뭐해요? ✗

chunks.note: V-는 걸 좋아해요 = I like doing V: 사진 찍는 걸, 요리하는 걸, 노래하는 걸 좋아해요.
chunks.common_mistake: 운동해요를 좋아해요 ✗ → 운동하는 걸 좋아해요 ✓: turn the verb into a noun first.

chunks.note: -(으)ㄹ래요? is a friendly invitation. Add a place: 같이 광안리에 갈래요? or an activity: 같이 밥 먹을래요?
chunks.common_mistake: 같이 가고 싶어요? ✗ (asks about their wish) → 같이 갈래요? ✓

chunks.en: Can you give me your KakaoTalk ID?
chunks.note: Almost everyone in Korea uses KakaoTalk (카톡). Many people just show their QR code.
chunks.common_mistake: 전화번호 줘 ✗: 반말 with someone you just met sounds rude. Stay with 해요체 until they suggest 말 놓을까요?

chunks.note: A warm way to end a meeting. Answer: 저도요! (Me too!)
chunks.common_mistake: 오늘 정말 즐거워요 (present) when leaving → use the past: 즐거웠어요.

roleplay.speaker: 친구
roleplay.task_en: Greet her and say it's nice to meet her.

roleplay.speaker: 친구
roleplay.task_en: Say you're from Vietnam.

roleplay.speaker: 친구
roleplay.prompt_en: Wow, your Korean is really good!
roleplay.task_en: Reply modestly to the compliment.

roleplay.speaker: 친구
roleplay.task_en: Say you like taking photos.

roleplay.speaker: 친구
roleplay.prompt_ko: 저는 요리하는 걸 좋아해요. 부산 맛집도 많이 알아요.
roleplay.prompt_en: I like cooking. I know lots of good restaurants in Busan, too.
roleplay.task_en: Suggest eating together sometime.

roleplay.speaker: 친구
roleplay.prompt_en: Great! How should we keep in touch?
roleplay.task_en: Ask for her KakaoTalk ID.

roleplay.speaker: 친구
roleplay.prompt_en: Then I'll message you this weekend! It was nice meeting you.
roleplay.task_en: Say you really enjoyed today.

situation_en: Your first week in the BUFS dorm: meet your roommate, find the laundry room, ask about quiet hours, and report a broken heater at the dorm office.

dialogue.speaker: 룸메이트
dialogue.en: Hi! Are you the new roommate?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Yes, nice to meet you. (I look forward to living with you.)

dialogue.speaker: 룸메이트
dialogue.ko: 저는 준호예요. 모르는 거 있으면 물어보세요.
dialogue.romanization: Jeoneun Junhoyeyo. Moreuneun geo isseumyeon mureoboseyo.
dialogue.en: I'm Junho. Ask me if there's anything you don't know.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 뭐 하나 물어봐도 돼요? 세탁실은 어디에 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: Mwo hana mureobwado dwaeyo? Setaksireun eodie isseoyo?
dialogue.en: Can I ask you something? Where's the laundry room?

dialogue.speaker: 룸메이트
dialogue.ko: 지하 1층에 있어요. 세제는 직접 사야 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: Jiha il cheunge isseoyo. Sejeneun jikjeop saya dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: In basement 1. You have to buy your own detergent.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 그리고 몇 시부터 조용히 해야 돼요?
dialogue.romanization: Geurigo myeot sibuteo joyonghi haeya dwaeyo?
dialogue.en: And from what time do we need to be quiet?

dialogue.speaker: 룸메이트
dialogue.en: From 11 at night.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Got it. Oh, the heater won't turn on.

dialogue.speaker: 룸메이트
dialogue.romanization: Il cheung haengjeongsire malhamyeon gochyeo jwoyo.
dialogue.en: Tell the office on the first floor and they'll fix it.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: (At the office) Hello. I'm in room 302, and the heater is broken.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Since when has it not worked?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 어제부터요. 오늘 고쳐 주실 수 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: Eojebuteoyo. Oneul gochyeo jusil su isseoyo?
dialogue.en: Since yesterday. Could you fix it today?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Yes, I'll come by this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Thank you!

chunks.en: Nice to meet you. (I look forward to working with you.)
chunks.note: Said when you start something together: new roommate, coworker, teammate, class.
chunks.common_mistake: There's no exact English; don't translate it word for word as 'please do well'.

chunks.note: -아/어도 돼요? asks for permission: 들어가도 돼요? (May I come in?)
chunks.common_mistake: 물어봐도 될까요? is even softer; 물어봐요 돼요 ✗.

chunks.note: 세탁실 = laundry room, 세탁기 = washing machine, 건조기 = dryer, 세제 = detergent.
chunks.common_mistake: 빨래방 is a paid laundromat outside, not the dorm laundry room.

alternatives: 밤에 몇 시부터 조용히 해야 돼요?
chunks.en: From what time do we have to be quiet?
chunks.note: -아/어야 돼요 = have to. 부터 = from, 까지 = until.
chunks.common_mistake: 몇 시에서 ✗ for 'from what time' → 몇 시부터 ✓

chunks.note: 켜지다 = to come on. 안 켜져요 = it won't come on. Also: 불이 안 켜져요 (the light).
chunks.common_mistake: 히터가 안 켜요 ✗ (that means 'the heater doesn't turn something on').

chunks.note: 고장 나다 = to break down (machines): 세탁기, 에어컨, 도어락.
chunks.common_mistake: 히터가 깨졌어요 ✗: 깨지다 means shattered, like glass.

chunks.note: -인데요 gives the background before your real point: 302호인데요, 히터가…
chunks.common_mistake: 302 방 ✗ → 302호 ✓ (호 is the counter for room numbers).

chunks.note: 부터 = since/from: 오늘 아침부터, 지난주부터.
chunks.common_mistake: 어제에서 ✗ → 어제부터 ✓

chunks.note: 고치다 = to fix. -아/어 주실 수 있어요? = polite request.
chunks.common_mistake: 수리해 주세요 is also fine; 고쳐요 주세요 ✗.

roleplay.speaker: 룸메이트
roleplay.prompt_en: Hi! Are you the new roommate?
roleplay.task_en: Say yes, and that you look forward to living together.

roleplay.speaker: 룸메이트
roleplay.task_en: Ask where the laundry room is.

roleplay.speaker: 룸메이트
roleplay.task_en: Ask from what time you have to be quiet.
accepted: 밤에 몇 시부터 조용히 해야 돼요?

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Say you're in room 405 and the washing machine is broken.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Since when has it not worked?
roleplay.task_en: Say since this morning.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Politely ask if they can fix it today.
accepted: 혹시 오늘 고쳐 주실 수 있어요?

title_en: Getting documents at the campus office
situation_en: Your visa expires soon, and the immigration office needs a certificate of enrollment. Go to the international office, ask for it in English, find out how long it takes, and ask where to print a transcript.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Hello. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: I'd like to get a certificate of enrollment.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Where will you submit it?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 비자 연장 때문에 필요해요. 출입국사무소에 내야 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: Bija yeonjang ttaemune piryohaeyo. Churipguksamuso-e naeya dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: I need it for my visa extension. I have to hand it in at the immigration office.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: Do you have your student ID?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Yes, here it is.

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.ko: 한국어로 해 드릴까요, 영어로 해 드릴까요?
dialogue.romanization: Hangugeoro hae deurilkkayo, yeongeoro hae deurilkkayo?
dialogue.en: Would you like it in Korean or in English?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 영어로 두 장 부탁드려요. 얼마나 걸려요?
dialogue.romanization: Yeongeoro du jang butakdeuryeoyo. Eolmana geollyeoyo?
dialogue.en: Two copies in English, please. How long does it take?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: About five minutes.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 혹시 성적증명서도 여기서 받을 수 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: Hoksi seongjeokjeungmyeongseodo yeogiseo badeul su isseoyo?
dialogue.en: By any chance, can I get a transcript here too?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: You can print transcripts at the self-service kiosk.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Sorry, could you say that again?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: The self-service kiosk. You can print it with your student ID.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Where is the kiosk?

dialogue.speaker: 직원
dialogue.en: On the first floor, next to the elevator.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Thank you. Have a good day.

chunks.en: I'd like to get a certificate of enrollment.
chunks.note: 발급받다 = to have a document issued. In everyday talk people also say 떼다: 재학증명서 떼러 왔어요.
chunks.common_mistake: 재학증명서를 사고 싶어요 ✗: you don't 'buy' a document. Use 발급받다 or 떼다.

chunks.en: I need it for my visa extension.
chunks.note: N 때문에 = because of N. Useful for any 'why do you need it?' question.
chunks.common_mistake: 비자를 늘리다 ✗ → 비자를 연장하다 ✓. 늘리다 is for making things bigger or longer, not documents.

chunks.note: What you say while handing something over: ID, card, money, a form.
chunks.common_mistake: 여기 있으세요 ✗ about your own things: -(으)시- honors the other person, never yourself.

chunks.note: 부탁드려요 is politer than 주세요: good at offices. 장 is the counter for sheets of paper.
chunks.common_mistake: 두 개 ✗ → 두 장 ✓ for documents and tickets.

chunks.note: 걸리다 = to take (time). The answer often uses 정도 (about): 5분 정도 걸려요.
chunks.common_mistake: 얼마 시간이에요? ✗ → 얼마나 걸려요? ✓

chunks.en: Can I get a transcript here too?
chunks.note: -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요? asks whether something is possible. 도 = also. 혹시 (by any chance) in front makes it softer.
chunks.common_mistake: 성적표 is the grade report you check online; the official document is 성적증명서.

chunks.note: 말씀하다 is the honorific of 말하다. Probably the most useful phrase in any office.
chunks.common_mistake: 다시 말해 ✗ (반말, sounds rude to staff) → 다시 한번 말씀해 주시겠어요? ✓

chunks.note: 무인 = unmanned. Many campus documents print from a kiosk with your student ID.
chunks.common_mistake: 어디에서 있어요? ✗ → 어디에 있어요? ✓: location of a thing uses 에, not 에서.

chunks.en: Thank you. Have a good day.
chunks.note: 수고하세요 ('keep up the work') is a common goodbye to staff who are still working.
chunks.common_mistake: Don't say 수고하세요 to a professor or someone senior: it can sound like you are judging their work. Use 감사합니다 or 안녕히 계세요.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Hello. How can I help you?
roleplay.task_en: Ask for a certificate of enrollment.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Say you need it to open a bank account.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Do you have your student ID?
roleplay.task_en: Say yes and hand it over.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_ko: 한국어로 해 드릴까요, 영어로 해 드릴까요?
roleplay.task_en: Ask for one copy in Korean.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.prompt_en: Fill in the form, take a number ticket and wait.
roleplay.task_en: That was fast. Politely ask them to say it again.

roleplay.speaker: 직원
roleplay.task_en: Thank them and say goodbye politely.

situation_en: You applied for a part-time job at a café. The owner interviews you. Use formal speech (합쇼체 -습니다/-ㅂ니다): it shows respect in interviews.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Welcome. What brings you here?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Hello. I'm here for the part-time job interview.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.ko: 아, 네. 앉으세요. 자기소개 좀 해 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: A, ne. Anjeuseyo. Jagisogae jom hae juseyo.
dialogue.en: Oh, yes. Have a seat. Please introduce yourself.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: I'm studying Korean at BUFS.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Have you ever worked at a café?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Yes, I have experience working at a café.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: When can you work?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 평일에는 저녁에 가능하고, 주말에도 일할 수 있습니다.
dialogue.romanization: Pyeongireneun jeonyeoge ganeunghago, jumaredo ilhal su itseumnida.
dialogue.en: I'm available on weekday evenings, and I can also work on weekends.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: You're an international student, right? Do you have a work permit?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.en: Yes, I have permission for part-time work.

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: Good. When can you start?

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 다음 주부터 일할 수 있습니다. 혹시 시급이 어떻게 되나요?
dialogue.romanization: Daeum jubuteo ilhal su itseumnida. Hoksi sigeubi eotteoke doenayo?
dialogue.en: I can start next week. May I ask what the hourly wage is?

dialogue.speaker: 사장님
dialogue.en: We pay the minimum wage.

dialogue.speaker: 나
dialogue.ko: 네, 알겠습니다. 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다.
dialogue.romanization: Ne, algetseumnida. Sigan nae jusyeoseo gamsahamnida.
dialogue.en: I see. Thank you for your time.

chunks.en: I'm here for the part-time job interview.
chunks.note: -(으)러 왔습니다 = 'I came to …'. 알바 is the casual short form of 아르바이트.
chunks.common_mistake: 면접을 하러 ✗ → 면접 보러 ✓. You 'see' (보다) an interview or exam: 시험 보다, 면접 보다.

chunks.note: -고 있습니다 = ongoing action ('am studying'). 부산외대 is the common short name.
chunks.common_mistake: 부산외대에 공부 ✗ → 부산외대에서 공부 ✓. Use 에서 for where an action happens.

chunks.en: I have experience working at a café.
chunks.note: -(으)ㄴ 경험이 있다 and -아/어 본 적이 있다 both mean 'have done before'.
chunks.common_mistake: 일하는 경험 ✗ → 일한 경험 ✓. Past experience uses the past modifier -(으)ㄴ.

chunks.en: I don't have experience, but I'll learn quickly.
chunks.note: -겠습니다 expresses will and sounds committed and polite: 열심히 하겠습니다!
chunks.common_mistake: Don't stop at 경험이 없습니다. Always add what you will do.

chunks.en: I can also work on weekends.
chunks.note: -(으)ㄹ 수 있습니다 = 'can'. 도 = 'also'. Weekend availability is a big plus for employers.
chunks.common_mistake: 가능합니다 alone is fine too, but the full sentence sounds more confident.

chunks.en: On weekdays I'm available in the evening.
chunks.note: 은/는 here contrasts weekdays with weekends. 오전 = morning, 오후 = afternoon.
chunks.common_mistake: 평일 = weekday, 평소 = usually. They sound similar.

chunks.en: I have permission for part-time work.
chunks.note: International students (D-2/D-4 visa) need 시간제 취업 허가 from immigration, applied for through the international office, before working.
chunks.common_mistake: Working without this permit can affect your visa. Get it before your first shift.

chunks.en: I can start from next week.
chunks.note: 부터 = 'from', 까지 = 'until'. 월요일부터 금요일까지.
chunks.common_mistake: 다음 주에서 ✗ → 다음 주부터 ✓. Time starting points use 부터.

chunks.note: N이/가 어떻게 되나요? is a soft, polite way to ask about money, age or schedule. Start with 혹시 (by any chance) to soften it more.
chunks.common_mistake: 시급이 얼마예요? is clear but more direct. In interviews, the softer form sounds better.

chunks.note: -아/어 주셔서 감사합니다 = 'thank you for doing …'. 도와주셔서 감사합니다 = thanks for helping.
chunks.common_mistake: 고마워요 is too casual to end an interview. Use 감사합니다.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.prompt_en: (Convenience store) Welcome. What brings you here?
roleplay.task_en: Say you came for the part-time job interview.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.prompt_en: Have you ever worked at a convenience store?
roleplay.task_en: Say you have no experience but will learn quickly.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.prompt_en: Can you work on weekends too?
roleplay.task_en: Say yes, you can work on weekends.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.prompt_ko: 외국인 학생이죠? 일할 수 있는 허가는 있어요?
roleplay.prompt_en: You're an international student, right? Do you have permission to work?
roleplay.task_en: Say yes, you have permission for part-time work.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Say you can start next week.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.task_en: Politely ask what the hourly wage is.

roleplay.speaker: 사장님
roleplay.prompt_en: Then I'll let you know the result tomorrow.
roleplay.task_en: Thank them for their time.
